documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time seen: 21:40, ED bay 7
CC: cough and shortness of breath x 3 days
HPI:
85 yo F with HTN, osteoarthritis, prior cholecystectomy presents with 3 days productive cough, yellow-green sputum, and progressive dyspnea.
Subjective fevers and chills at home, no measured temp. Poor appetite x 2 days.
Nausea with 4 episodes of non-bloody emesis today, unable to keep fluids or pills down.
Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, leg swelling, or calf pain.
Daughter at bedside reports pt is at her usual baseline and fully oriented, conversing normally.
No recent travel. No sick contacts known. Lives alone in single-story home, independent with ADLs, uses cane outdoors.
ROS: positive for cough, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, fatigue. Negative for dysuria, diarrhea, rash, headache.
PMH:
Hypertension
Osteoarthritis, bilateral knees
Remote cholecystectomy
Osteopenia
Home meds:
amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h prn
vitamin D 1000 units PO daily
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Social: never smoker. No alcohol. Widowed, daughter lives 10 min away.
Family hx: noncontributory
VITALS AT TRIAGE:
T 38.4 C, HR 104, BP 128/68, respiratory rate 24, SpO2 87% on RA
Placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93% after 10 min.
Repeat at 4 hours: T 37.9, HR 92, BP 122/70, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 94% on 3L NC
EXAM:
Gen: elderly female, mildly tachypneic at rest, speaking in full sentences
HEENT: dry mucous membranes
Neck: no JVD, no adenopathy
Lungs: crackles right base and right mid axillary line, dullness to percussion right base, no wheeze
CV: RRR, no murmur, no edema
Abd: soft, nontender, BS present, well healed RUQ scar
Ext: no calf tenderness
Skin: warm, dry, no rash
Neuro: alert, follows commands, moves all extremities, gait not tested
LABS:
WBC 15.2 with 84% neutrophils, Hgb 11.8, Plt 244
Na 133, K 3.6, Cl 98, CO2 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 118
Lactate 1.6, CRP 128
Blood cultures x2 drawn prior to antibiotics. Resp viral panel sent. Urine strep and legionella antigens sent.
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
ASSESSMENT:
85 yo F with community acquired pneumonia, hypoxemic, with vomiting and poor PO intake.
CURB-65 of 1, scored for age only. BUN, BP, respiratory rate and mental status criteria not met.
Admit to medical floor given hypoxemia and inability to tolerate PO.
PLAN:
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin 500 mg daily.
Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting - keep all meds IV for now.
O2 3L NC, titrate to SpO2 >92%
NS 75 mL/hr x 12h then reassess
Ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h prn nausea
Hold lisinopril while volume depleted; continue amlodipine when PO tolerated
Acetaminophen 650 mg IV/PO q6h prn fever
Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, OOB to chair with assist
Repeat CBC/BMP in AM, trend O2 requirement
DVT ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily
Code status: full, confirmed with pt and daughter

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD2, 07:35
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports cough somewhat looser overnight. Slept in 2 hours blocks. Two episodes of emesis overnight at 01:20 and 04:50.
Still unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting - took sips of water only, brought up crackers.
Denies chest pain. Dyspnea improved with rest but present with ambulation to bathroom.
OBJECTIVE:
T max 38.1 overnight, current T 37.4, HR 88, BP 118/64, RR 20
Still on 3L NC, SpO2 94%. Desats to 90% walking to bathroom with RN.
I/O: in 1850 mL, out 1100 mL. No stool.
Exam: crackles persist right base, slightly less coarse mid lung. No accessory muscle use. Abd soft. Alert and conversant, at baseline.
Labs: WBC 12.6 (from 15.2), Hgb 11.4, Plt 238, Na 135, K 3.8, BUN 15, Cr 0.8
Blood cultures NGTD at 24h. Resp viral panel negative. Urine legionella negative.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:

1. CAP, RLL/RML with small right effusion - clinically improving, WBC trending down. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. No indication for thoracentesis, effusion small and free flowing.
2. Hypoxemia - remains on 3L NC. Wean as tolerated, goal SpO2 >92%. Incentive spirometry reinforced with RN.
3. Nausea/vomiting - continue IV route for all meds. Scheduled ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h today instead of prn. Clear liquid trial this afternoon.
4. Volume - continue NS at 75 mL/hr, reassess at 16:00.
5. HTN - lisinopril still held, BP acceptable. Amlodipine held while NPO.
6. DVT ppx enoxaparin continues. Mobilize to chair TID with PT eval ordered.
Daughter updated at bedside 08:10.
Attending discussed and agrees with plan.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD3, 08:05
SUBJECTIVE:
Much better day. No emesis in past 20 hours. Tolerated full clear liquids and half a breakfast tray this morning.
Cough less frequent, productive of thinner sputum. Walked hallway with PT yesterday evening.
OBJECTIVE:
Afebrile x 26 hours. T 36.9, HR 78, BP 126/70, RR 18
Weaned to 2L NC at 22:40 last night, then to room air at 06:15 this AM with SpO2 93% at rest, 91% ambulating 100 feet.
I/O: in 1600 mL, out 1500 mL.
Exam: fewer crackles right base, no dullness change. No respiratory distress. Speaking in full sentences. Alert, oriented, engaged in conversation.
Labs: WBC 9.4, Hgb 11.2, Na 137, K 4.0, BUN 12, Cr 0.8, CRP 72
Blood cultures negative at 48h. Urine strep pneumo antigen positive.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. CAP - streptococcal, responding well. Transition off IV: stop azithromycin, narrow to amoxicillin 1 g PO TID now that PO tolerated. Total course 5 days.
2. Small right pleural effusion - asymptomatic, no repeat imaging needed unless fever recurs.
3. Hypoxemia - resolved, off O2. Ambulatory sat check this afternoon prior to planning discharge.
4. Nausea - resolved. Discontinue scheduled ondansetron, leave prn.
5. HTN - restart amlodipine 5 mg PO daily today. Resume lisinopril 10 mg PO daily tomorrow if Cr stable.
6. PT: recommends home with cane, daughter to stay first 2 nights.
7. Nutrition: regular diet advanced, encourage intake.
Anticipate discharge tomorrow if maintaining sats on RA and eating.
IV fluids discontinued 08:30.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD4
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD4. Total LOS 4 days.
Discharge diagnosis: community acquired pneumonia, right lower and right middle lobe, with small right pleural effusion
Secondary: hypertension, osteoarthritis, osteopenia
HOSPITAL COURSE:
85 yo F admitted with 3 days of cough, dyspnea, fever and vomiting.
At triage: respiratory rate 24, SpO2 87% on RA; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 20 at 4 hours.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
CURB-65 of 1 at admission, scored for age only.
Started on ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so all meds given IV with ondansetron and NS.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2 with WBC down from 15.2 to 12.6.
Vomiting resolved HD3, PO intake resumed. Weaned to room air HD3 at 06:15 with SpO2 93% at rest.
Urine strep pneumoniae antigen positive. Blood cultures x2 no growth at discharge. Legionella antigen and respiratory viral panel negative.
Narrowed to oral amoxicillin HD3. Afebrile since HD2 evening.
HD4: WBC 8.1, Cr 0.8, ambulatory SpO2 94% on RA over 250 feet. Eating full meals. Ready for discharge home.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.8, HR 76, BP 124/72, RR 17, SpO2 94% RA
DISCHARGE EXAM: comfortable, mild scattered right basilar crackles, no distress, alert and conversant, ambulating with cane.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
amoxicillin 1 g PO TID to complete through 2 more days
amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h prn pain or fever
vitamin D 1000 units PO daily
ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h prn nausea, 6 tablets
Allergies: sulfa - rash
FOLLOW UP:
Primary care clinic in 5 to 7 days for reassessment and pulse ox check.
Repeat chest x-ray in 6 weeks to document resolution of infiltrate and effusion.
INSTRUCTIONS:
Use incentive spirometer 10 times per hour while awake.
Return to ED for fever above 38.0, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
Daughter to stay with pt for first 2 nights, present for discharge teaching at 11:15.
Discharged home HD4 at 12:30 ambulatory with daughter.
